title: The First Night: Deny Trauma
coreMove: Treat a painful backstory as context, then ask what the present pattern still accomplishes before granting it authority.
sourcePressure: The source supports the first night as an anti-fatalism opener: people can change, anger may be purposive, self-dislike can be protective, and denying trauma means denying destiny, not denying pain.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says trauma is fake or that hurt people should simply choose better; the correct version respects pain while refusing to let history become the final explanation.

sourceAnchors.name: Alfred Adler
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source identifies the book as drawing on Adlerian psychology and includes the visible first-night heading 'Socrates and Adler'.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Adlerian freedom starts to bite when the old wound is no longer allowed to be the whole trial, judge, and sentence.

sourceAnchors.name: Socrates
sourceAnchors.detail: The authorized preview headings include 'Socrates and Adler' inside the first night.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Socratic pressure is not comfort; it is the steady refusal to stop at the first explanation that makes you feel finished.

hook: Your past is not your prison
The wound does not define you
Everything changes when you realize trauma is a choice
counterintuition: Most people think the past controls them
The opposite of trauma is choice
tryThisNow: Spend five minutes journaling about your past
Set a timer and choose a new story
examples: coach telling someone to toughen up

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital charge-nurse apology after a snapped handoff
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinical lead who keeps excusing sharpness as the inevitable residue of a brutal residency
exampleSpecs.stakes: a new nurse may stop asking questions during medication handoff if the old excuse keeps ending the conversation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Camille starts to say the residency made her this way, stops, and writes down what the snap accomplished in the room: silence from the junior nurse and protection from embarrassment.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "I learned this in residency," Camille says with the narcotics log still open between them.

exampleSpecs.domain: conservatory audition avoidance after an old humiliation
exampleSpecs.audience: a trained musician who has turned one failed teenage audition into a permanent rule against trying
exampleSpecs.stakes: a chamber ensemble slot closes tonight and the self-protective identity may cost him the only opening this year
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: James places the unsubmitted audition recording beside the old rejection letter and admits the old story now protects him from hearing a fresh no.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Rosin dust hangs over the black violin case.

exampleSpecs.domain: tenant association chair using anger to stop a budget question
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer leader who calls every raised voice a natural response to being disrespected
exampleSpecs.stakes: a leaking roof vote will fail if budget questions keep getting shut down by intimidation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It takes Hanna three meetings to see that her anger arrives exactly when someone asks for receipts, and that the outburst ends scrutiny every time.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Three sets of meeting minutes are spread across Hanna's dining table.

exampleSpecs.domain: junior hockey referee protecting pride after a missed call
exampleSpecs.audience: a young official who hides inside the story that he grew up being challenged by loud adults
exampleSpecs.stakes: one avoidable ejection may cost him a playoff assignment and teach the rink that his whistle is about pride
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Diego watches the video with the sound off, marks the exact second he ejects the coach, and sees that the anger protected him from admitting the missed offside.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The rink camera shows only fogged glass and a red circle around the blue line.

exampleSpecs.domain: ceramics studio owner clinging to a small identity after a failed shop
exampleSpecs.audience: a craft entrepreneur who calls herself bad with money to avoid reopening in a smaller, safer format
exampleSpecs.stakes: a low-rent shared kiln slot expires while the protective identity keeps her from trying again
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marta asks what the phrase 'I am hopeless with money' has saved her from doing this month and circles the unanswered email about the shared kiln.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What has the sentence saved you from this week?

exampleSpecs.domain: adult language learner using family history to avoid speaking practice
exampleSpecs.audience: a newcomer who has a real history of being mocked for pronunciation and now treats silence as fixed identity
exampleSpecs.stakes: a licensing interview is six weeks away and every skipped conversation makes the old protection stronger
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Akira leave the community-center conversation table early, then make him name what silence protected today: not from pain in general, but from one visible mistake in front of strangers.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You hear the plastic chair legs scrape before the practice round is over.

skillTargets: distinguish respecting pain from granting pain final authority
identify what anger or self-dislike accomplishes in a concrete situation
choose a response that asks present-purpose questions without blaming suffering
separate cause-based explanation from purpose-based analysis

tryThisNowSpec: Take one behavior you usually explain with a backstory and write one sentence naming what it protected in the last 24 hours.
